```{r setup, include=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
run_examples <- identical(Sys.getenv("DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_VIGNETTE"), "true")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval=run_examples, collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5, out.width="100%",
                     dpi=150, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
if (run_examples) {
  library(dgpsi)
  backend <- Sys.getenv("DGPSI_TUTORIAL_BACKEND")
  if (nzchar(backend)) init_py(dgpsi_ver=backend, verb=FALSE) else init_py(verb=FALSE)
  set_thread_num(1)
}
```

A linked emulator passes intermediate predictions and their uncertainty to
downstream models. Some of these inputs may add little predictive value.
`prunlgp()` evaluates reduced input sets, refits the receiving models and selects
a network using validation predictions from the whole system.

The example uses the development R interface and Python backend recorded in
[the validation notes](https://github.com/zhuangchaoqun/dgpsi-R/blob/prunlgp/VALIDATION.md). The data and fitting settings are fixed
before selection.

This example starts with six internal connections. Two intermediate emulators,
`u` and `v`, supply three downstream emulators, `a`, `b` and `c`. Each output has its own
DGP and selects its own subset of the two internal inputs.

## Load the data

The accompanying file contains a small, de-identified sample of operational
measurements: 96 training rows, 48 validation rows and 96 test rows from consecutive,
non-overlapping periods. Variable names are neutral and timestamps and equipment
identifiers have been removed. A one-sided filter was applied before sampling;
the example therefore evaluates filtered responses. All columns were centred and
scaled using the **training rows only**, then rounded to six decimal places.

`x1`--`x16` are global inputs available under the example's prediction information
set. These include origin measurements and prescribed boundary inputs. They do
not include future observations of `u`, `v`, `a`, `b` or `c`. The observed intermediate
responses are used to train components; validation and test predictions receive
only the global inputs.

```{r data, purl=FALSE}
library(dgpsi)
library(ggplot2)
dat <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "prunlgp_example.csv", package="dgpsi"))
train <- subset(dat, split == "train")
validation <- subset(dat, split == "validation")
test <- subset(dat, split == "test")
global <- paste0("x", 1:16)
table(dat$split)
```

For a new dataset, estimate transformation parameters on the training partition
and apply those same parameters to validation and test data. Standardisation is
a numerical transformation, not a guarantee of anonymity.

## Train the component emulators

Each downstream component initially receives both internal inputs. We use the
same DGP architecture and fitting budget before and after pruning: two layers,
two latent nodes, 40 iterations, ten ESS burn-in steps per iteration and five
imputations. The burn-in count is explicit because development versions may
use different defaults.

```{r fit, purl=FALSE}
features <- list(
  u = c("x1", "x2", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x9", "x10"),
  v = c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x11", "x12"),
  a = c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "u", "v"),
  b = c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "u", "v"),
  c = c("x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "u", "v")
)
components <- lapply(names(features), function(id) {
  set_seed(57)
  dgp(as.matrix(train[, features[[id]]]), as.matrix(train[, id, drop=FALSE]),
      id=id, name="sexp", depth=2, node=2, N=40, B=5, ess_burn=10,
      share=FALSE, bounds=c(0.1, 10), prior="ga", nugget_est=TRUE, verb=FALSE)
})
```

## Construct the initial network

`To_Input` identifies the receiving component's training column. An internal
connection takes output 1 of `u` or `v`; a global connection takes the corresponding
column of the supplied global input matrix.

```{r link, purl=FALSE}
connections <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(features), function(id) {
  f <- features[[id]]
  internal <- f %in% c("u", "v")
  data.frame(
    From_Emulator=ifelse(internal, f, "Global"),
    To_Emulator=id,
    From_Output=ifelse(internal, 1L, match(f, global)),
    To_Input=seq_along(f)
  )
}))
network <- lgp(connections, components, B=5, verb=FALSE)
```

## Select internal connections

The `refit` function states exactly how a reduced component is trained. Its
`keep` argument refers to columns of the **original** training matrix; it never
refers to an already reduced matrix. The component's response and ID are retained.

```{r refit, purl=FALSE}
refit <- function(model, keep, seed) {
  dgpsi::set_seed(seed)
  dgpsi::dgp(model$data$X[, keep, drop=FALSE], model$data$Y,
      id=model$id, name="sexp", depth=2, node=2, N=40, B=5, ess_burn=10,
      share=FALSE, bounds=c(0.1, 10), prior="ga", nugget_est=TRUE, verb=FALSE)
}
```

Here the system objective is the equally weighted mean normalised RMSE of `a`,
`b` and `c`. The normalising scales are computed from their component training
responses. `u` and `v` still participate in linked prediction, but are not scored
in this particular objective.

```{r prune, purl=FALSE}
selected <- prunlgp(
  network, components,
  x=as.matrix(validation[, global]),
  y=lapply(validation[, c("a", "b", "c")], as.numeric),
  refit=refit, seed=57, B=5, search="subsets",
  max_rounds=2, max_evals=32, verb=FALSE
)
selected
```

At each visit, the function evaluates all internal-input subsets for the receiving
output while holding other fitted components fixed. It then compares the
**system** validation losses. The initial network and the network without
internal inputs are also candidates. The best admissible evaluated network is
returned. This extends output-specific subset selection with a system-level
objective; it does not claim to solve the global combinatorial optimisation problem.

```{r history, purl=FALSE}
knitr::kable(selected$history[, c("evaluation", "stage", "loss", "internal_links",
                                "admissible", "selected")], digits=4)
```

## Inspect the networks

Both objects below are ordinary linked emulators. The initial model is activated
with the same settings used during selection, providing a consistent reference
for the subsequent comparison. Blue arrows show retained internal connections;
orange dashed arrows show deleted connections in the initial graph. Grey arrows
represent global inputs. Node positions are identical in both views.

```{r network-before, purl=FALSE}
network_view <- function(model, title) {
  view <- summary(model)
  view$height <- "440px"
  view$x$height <- "360px"
  view$x$main$text <- title
  view$x$submain$text <- ""
  view$x$footer$text <- ""
  view$x$nodes$label <- ifelse(view$x$nodes$id == "Global", "Global",
                              paste0(view$x$nodes$id, "\nDGP"))
  view$x$nodes$shape <- ifelse(view$x$nodes$id == "Global", "database", "box")
  view$x$nodes$color <- ifelse(view$x$nodes$id=="Global", "#67B7F7",
    ifelse(view$x$nodes$id %in% c("u", "v"), "#F2767A", "#6DB66E"))
  position <- data.frame(id=c("Global", "u", "v", "a", "b", "c"),
                         x=c(0, 220, 220, 440, 440, 440),
                         y=c(0, -100, 100, -140, 0, 140))
  index <- match(view$x$nodes$id, position$id)
  view$x$nodes$x <- position$x[index]
  view$x$nodes$y <- position$y[index]
  edge_key <- paste(view$x$edges$from, view$x$edges$to)
  kept_key <- paste(selected$structure$From_Emulator, selected$structure$To_Emulator)
  internal <- view$x$edges$from != "Global"
  removed <- internal & !edge_key %in% kept_key
  view$x$edges$color <- ifelse(!internal, "#BBBBBB",
                              ifelse(removed, "#D55E00", "#0072B2"))
  view$x$edges$dashes <- removed
  view$x$edges$width <- ifelse(internal, 2, 1)
  view <- visNetwork::visHierarchicalLayout(view, enabled=FALSE)
  view <- visNetwork::visPhysics(view, enabled=FALSE)
  view <- visNetwork::visNodes(view, font=list(color="black", size=16))
  htmlwidgets::onRender(view, "function(el, x) {
    document.getElementById('maindiv' + el.id).style.height = 'calc(100% - 80px)';
  }")
}
network_view(selected$initial_model, "Before pruning: six internal connections")
```

```{r network-after, purl=FALSE}
n_links <- sum(selected$structure$From_Emulator != "Global")
network_view(selected, sprintf("After pruning: %d internal %s", n_links,
  if(n_links == 1) "connection" else "connections"))
```

```{r retained, purl=FALSE}
original_edges <- subset(selected$initial_structure, From_Emulator != "Global")
retained_edges <- subset(selected$structure, From_Emulator != "Global")
connection_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("a", "b", "c"), function(id) {
  original <- original_edges$From_Emulator[original_edges$To_Emulator == id]
  retained <- retained_edges$From_Emulator[retained_edges$To_Emulator == id]
  removed <- setdiff(original, retained)
  data.frame(output=id, initial=length(original), retained=length(retained),
    removed=length(removed),
    retained_inputs=if(length(retained)) paste(retained, collapse=", ") else "None",
    removed_inputs=if(length(removed)) paste(removed, collapse=", ") else "None")
}))
knitr::kable(connection_summary, row.names=FALSE)
```

Pruning removes an input column and its connection. It does not remove the output
model or automatically disconnect other receivers. A model with no internal
inputs continues to use its global inputs and may still supply downstream models.

## Evaluate held-out predictions

Test responses are evaluated after structure selection. Neither the structure
search nor the component fitting uses them. The sample is an illustrative
benchmark, rather than a new prospective evaluation.

```{r test, purl=FALSE}
set_seed(57)
before <- predict(selected$initial_model, as.matrix(test[, global]),
                  full_layer=TRUE)$results
set_seed(57)
after <- predict(selected, as.matrix(test[, global]), full_layer=TRUE)$results
means <- function(p) do.call(c, unname(p$mean))
scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("a", "b", "c"), function(id) {
  data.frame(output=id,
    validation_unpruned=selected$initial_rmse[id],
    validation_pruned=selected$rmse[id],
    test_unpruned=sqrt(mean((as.numeric(means(before)[[id]])-test[[id]])^2)),
    test_pruned=sqrt(mean((as.numeric(means(after)[[id]])-test[[id]])^2)))
}))
scores$validation_reduction_pct <- 100*(1-scores$validation_pruned/scores$validation_unpruned)
scores$test_reduction_pct <- 100*(1-scores$test_pruned/scores$test_unpruned)
score_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("validation", "test"), function(part) {
  data.frame(Partition=part, Output=scores$output,
    Unpruned=scores[[paste0(part, "_unpruned")]],
    Pruned=scores[[paste0(part, "_pruned")]],
    Reduction=scores[[paste0(part, "_reduction_pct")]])
}))
knitr::kable(score_table, digits=c(0, 0, 4, 4, 2), row.names=FALSE,
             col.names=c("Partition", "Output", "Unpruned", "Pruned", "Reduction (%)"))
system_test <- c(Unpruned=mean(scores$test_unpruned / selected$settings$scale),
                 Pruned=mean(scores$test_pruned / selected$settings$scale))
knitr::kable(data.frame(model=names(system_test), mean_NRMSE=system_test),
             digits=4, row.names=FALSE)
```

```{r error-plot, fig.cap="Validation and test errors of the three scored outputs. Lower values are better.", purl=FALSE}
plot_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("validation", "test"), function(part) {
  rbind(data.frame(output=scores$output, partition=part, model="Unpruned",
                   RMSE=scores[[paste0(part, "_unpruned")]]),
        data.frame(output=scores$output, partition=part, model="Pruned",
                   RMSE=scores[[paste0(part, "_pruned")]]))
}))
plot_data$partition <- factor(plot_data$partition, levels=c("validation", "test"))
plot_data$model <- factor(plot_data$model, levels=c("Unpruned", "Pruned"))
ggplot(plot_data, aes(output, RMSE, fill=model)) +
  geom_col(position=position_dodge(0.7), width=0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.3f", RMSE)), position=position_dodge(0.7),
            vjust=-0.35, size=3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0, .14))) +
  facet_wrap(~partition) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c(Unpruned="#999999", Pruned="#0072B2")) +
  labs(x="Output", y="RMSE (standardised response)", fill=NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size=11) + theme(legend.position="top", panel.grid.minor=element_blank())
```

```{r comparison-text, echo=FALSE, results='asis', purl=FALSE}
cat(sprintf("The selected network reduces the validation objective by %.1f%% while retaining %d of the six internal links. Its mean test NRMSE is %.4f, compared with %.4f before pruning.\n\n",
  100*(1-selected$score/selected$initial_score),
  sum(selected$structure$From_Emulator!="Global"),
  system_test["Pruned"],system_test["Unpruned"]))
```

The validation objective determines the selected graph. A smaller validation
loss does not imply that every output, or the held-out test period, will improve.
The tables report both partitions so that this distinction remains visible.
Setting `protect=0` imposes a different search by rejecting candidates
whose scored validation outputs exceed their initial RMSEs.

The connection table and error plot answer different questions: which inputs
were removed, and how the resulting predictions changed. Different receivers
can retain different subsets of the same upstream outputs. An unchanged subset
can also yield unchanged predictions when its ancestors and fitted model remain
unchanged. Use explicit output protection when the application requires it.

## Check predictive intervals

Pruning leaves native uncertainty propagation in place. The following table
reports 95% moment-matched interval coverage, width and interval score on the
same test rows. Coverage should be assessed against 95%; width and interval
score are better when smaller at adequate coverage. These diagnostics are
reported after selection and do not enter the RMSE objective.

```{r intervals, purl=FALSE}
interval_summary <- function(p, label) {
  mu <- means(p); variance <- do.call(c, unname(p$var))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("a", "b", "c"), function(id) {
    lo <- as.numeric(mu[[id]]) - qnorm(.975)*sqrt(as.numeric(variance[[id]]))
    hi <- as.numeric(mu[[id]]) + qnorm(.975)*sqrt(as.numeric(variance[[id]]))
    truth <- test[[id]]; s <- selected$settings$scale[id]
    data.frame(model=label, output=id, coverage=mean(truth>=lo & truth<=hi),
      normalised_width=mean(hi-lo)/s,
      normalised_IS95=mean(hi-lo+40*pmax(lo-truth,0)+40*pmax(truth-hi,0))/s)
  }))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(interval_summary(before,"Unpruned"),
                  interval_summary(after,"Pruned")), digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

## Change the selection rule

Give a more important output a larger weight, or require every scored output to
stay within 1% of its initial validation RMSE. These are modelling choices to
make before examining test results.

```{r alternatives, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
protected <- prunlgp(network, components,
  as.matrix(validation[, global]), lapply(validation[, c("a", "b", "c")], as.numeric),
  refit, weights=c(a=1, b=1, c=2), protect=0.01, seed=57)

# For more candidate inputs, backward deletion reduces the search cost.
backward <- prunlgp(network, components,
  as.matrix(validation[, global]), lapply(validation[, c("a", "b", "c")], as.numeric),
  refit, search="backward", max_evals=100, seed=57)
```

Independent candidates can run on separate PSOCK workers. Keep the worker count
times the thread count within the available CPU budget. If a non-default Python
environment is used, supply the corresponding initialiser through `worker_init`.

```{r parallel, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
parallel_result <- prunlgp(network, components,
  as.matrix(validation[, global]), lapply(validation[, c("a", "b", "c")], as.numeric),
  refit, seed=57, workers=2, threads=1,
  worker_init=function() dgpsi::init_py(verb=FALSE))
```

For a time-expanded network, use `groups` to tie copies of the same fitted scalar
component. A removed dimension then disappears from every copy, including an
origin copy supplied by a measurement. Copies must have identical training data
and consistent original input positions. The caller is responsible for supplying
only global inputs available at the forecast origin or prescribed as known
boundaries; the function cannot infer measurement availability from numeric matrices.

The returned `$model` supports the usual linked prediction and plotting methods.
Use `dgpsi::serialize(selected$model, light=FALSE)` to save its Python-backed
state, and save `$history` and `$settings` alongside it for an audit of selection.

To execute all computations when rebuilding this article, set
`DGPSI_RUN_PRUNLGP_VIGNETTE=true` before calling `rmarkdown::render()`.
An optional `DGPSI_TUTORIAL_BACKEND` value is forwarded to `init_py(dgpsi_ver=...)`.
The default package build shows the code without starting or installing Python.
